<div class="alert alert-info">
**Note:**
This feature is currently under development. Its behaviour may change without notice.
</div>

`dv.manager` can offer a third, chat-based way of selecting the population/rows shown to modules,
powered by the [`querychat`](https://posit-dev.github.io/querychat/r/) package. Instead of building
a filter with the Filter or Subgroup tabs, users describe the subpopulation they want in natural
language (e.g. *"subjects over 30 who had a serious adverse event"*), and the chat translates that
request into a SQL query, applying the resulting subject IDs exactly like the existing population
filter.

## Enabling the feature

Set `enable_querychat = TRUE` in the `run_app()` call. This requires:

- The `querychat` package (>= 0.3.0) to be installed.
- `filter_dataset_name` and `filter_key` to be set (the same subject/population dataset and join
  key already used by the regular Filter tab).
- A configured LLM client/credentials for `querychat` itself (see querychat's own
  ["Models" article](https://posit-dev.github.io/querychat/r/) for API key setup) — this is not
  validated by `dv.manager` at startup, only when the chat is actually used.

```r
run_app(
  data = my_data,
  filter_dataset_name = "adsl",
  filter_key = "USUBJID",
  enable_querychat = TRUE,
  querychat_args = list(
    greeting = "Ask me about the population you'd like to see, e.g. \"subjects over 30\"."
  )
)
```

`querychat_args` is a named list forwarded to `querychat::QueryChat$new()`. Common entries:

- `client` — which LLM/model to use (see querychat's "Choosing a model" article).
- `greeting` — an initial assistant message shown to the user.
- `data_description` — a text description of the data handed to the LLM. If not supplied,
  `dv.manager` builds one automatically describing every dataset in the current `dataset_list`
  besides the subject/population dataset (see "How cross-dataset questions work" below).
- `extra_instructions`, `categorical_threshold` — see `?querychat::QueryChat`.

## How cross-dataset questions work

A `dataset_list` in `dv.manager` frequently contains more than one dataset (e.g. `adsl` for
subject-level data, `adae` for adverse events). To answer natural questions that span more than
one dataset, `dv.manager`:

1. Writes **every** dataset in the currently selected `dataset_list` into one shared, in-memory
   database connection.
2. Registers only the subject/population dataset (`filter_dataset_name`) as `querychat`'s "primary"
   table — this is the table whose schema `querychat` automatically describes to the LLM, and the
   one its filtering tool always returns full rows from.
3. Describes the other tables' columns to the LLM via `data_description`, with instructions to
   express population-defining criteria as `SELECT * FROM <subject_table> WHERE ... AND
   <filter_key> IN (SELECT <filter_key> FROM <other_table> WHERE ...)`.

Because the underlying database connection contains every table, the LLM's generated SQL can still
freely join or subquery across all of them — the chat only needs to resolve, in the end, to a
subject ID (`filter_key`) selection from the primary table. This subject ID set is then intersected
(AND'd) with whatever the Filter tab and Subgroup tab already select — the chat can only narrow the
population further, never widen it.

## Dataset-switch behaviour

`querychat` has no supported way of swapping the data source of an already-running chat instance.
Because of this, switching the active `dataset_list` at runtime **fully resets the chat** — a fresh
database connection is created and the conversation transcript starts over. This is a deliberate
trade-off: there is currently no API in `querychat` that would allow preserving the transcript while
safely swapping in a different set of tables.

## What data is sent to the LLM provider

With `enable_querychat = TRUE`, the LLM provider configured for `querychat` receives:

- Schema/column metadata (column names, types, and — for low-cardinality columns — the list of
  distinct values) for the subject/population dataset and, via the generated `data_description`,
  column names for every other dataset in the `dataset_list`.
- The text of the user's chat messages.

Raw row-level data is **not** sent to the LLM as part of ordinary operation; only the generated SQL
is executed locally against the shared database connection. Review this with your data governance
process before enabling this feature on datasets containing sensitive information.

## FAQ

- **Can I ask about adverse events even though I'm filtering subjects?** Yes — every dataset in the
  `dataset_list` is written into the same database connection and can be referenced in
  subqueries/joins; phrase your question in terms of subjects for best results, e.g. *"subjects who
  had a serious adverse event"*.
- **Does switching the dataset selector reset my chat?** Yes, see "Dataset-switch behaviour" above.
- **Does bookmarking work?** Yes — `querychat`'s own bookmarking support (`enable_bookmarking =
  TRUE`) persists and restores the chat's SQL/title state.
- **Can the chat modify or delete data?** No — `dv.manager` restricts `querychat` to its `"filter"`
  tool set, which only allows read-only `SELECT` queries; DDL/DML statements are rejected.
- **Is this enabled by default?** No, `enable_querychat` defaults to `FALSE`.
